specialism.name: documentation
specialism.task: Improve the clarity, consistency, and technical correctness of markdown documentation pages under the docs source directory (typically docs/src/). Work targets prose quality, heading hierarchy, Documenter.jl cross-reference syntax, and tone — not code examples or API listings, which belong to the docstrings specialism. The output of this specialism is documentation that reads consistently across pages, follows the tone established by the project and its ecosystem, and builds without Documenter.jl warnings.

workflow.step: Orient yourself. Read the project's docs build file (make.jl or equivalent) to learn: the checkdocs setting, sidebar page order, deploy target, and any custom plugins. Note which pages are listed so you know the intended coverage.

Detect the established tone and conventions. Read 1–2 existing pages that appear most complete. Note: voice (first/second/third person), heading case (sentence vs title), how code blocks are tagged, how cross-references are written (bare @ref vs. named @ref), and where lists vs. prose are preferred.

List all markdown files under the docs source directory: find docs/src -name '*.md' For each file, read it and identify: heading hierarchy violations, inconsistent voice or tone, missing language tags on code fences, broken or non-Documenter cross-references, and prose that is unclear, redundant, or off-tone. Do not invent new sections; focus on improving what exists.

Edit pages in place, applying the detected conventions from step 2. When tone is ambiguous, match the style of the most polished existing page. Flag any structural changes (new sections, page additions) for user approval before implementing them.
If authorized, build the docs locally: julia --project=docs docs/make.jl Resolve any new warnings introduced by the edits. Do not proceed past this step if the build emits errors.

rubric.criterion: All edited pages share the same voice and register as the baseline detected in step 2.
Each page has exactly one H1 (the page title); sub-headings are H2/H3 and never skip levels.
Cross-references use Documenter.jl @ref form. Code blocks carry a language tag. No bare URL links where @ref is appropriate.
The docs build (if run) produces no more warnings after the edit than before.
Only content already present is edited. New sections or pages require explicit user approval.

formatting.rule: ATX headings (# style), sentence-case (capitalize only first word and proper nouns).
Second-person voice for instructional content ("you can", "run the following").
Code fences must carry a language tag: ```julia, ```sh, ```toml, etc.
Inline code for symbol names, file paths, and short commands: `MyType`, `make.jl`.
Reference-style links only when the same URL is reused more than once on a page.
Cross-references to documented symbols: [`MyType`](@ref) or [custom text](@ref MyType).
No trailing whitespace; no hard line-breaks inside paragraphs (let the renderer wrap).
formatting.example:
## Before
# Getting Started
To install ClimaFoo, open Julia and type: ``` using Pkg; Pkg.add("ClimaFoo") ```
See also [the API](api.md) and [StaticEnvironment](../src/Environments.jl).
## After
# Getting started
To install ClimaFoo, open Julia and run:
```julia using Pkg Pkg.add("ClimaFoo") ```
See also the [API reference](@ref) and [`StaticEnvironment`](@ref).
